ceramic.title: Originator Controlled (ORCON) — Definition & Meaning
ceramic.snippet:
Originator Controlled , abbreviated ORCON and formally rendered \"Dissemination and Extraction of Information Controlled by Originator,\" is a dissemination control marking applied to U.S. classified national intelligence to retain the originating agencys authority over onward sharing. Its legal foundation rests in Executive Order 13526 (signed by President Barack Obama on 29 December 2009), which governs classified national security information, and in Intelligence Community Directive (ICD) 710, \"Classification Management and Control Markings System,\" issued by the Director of National Intelligence. The specific catalogue of authorized control markings, including ORCON, is maintained in the Controlled Access Program Coordination Office (CAPCO) Register and Manual, which the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) updates periodically. ORCON is one of several \"dissemination controls\" — alongside NOFORN, PROPIN, RELIDO, and FISA — that operate independently of the underlying classification level (Confidential, Secret, or Top Secret).

possession, knowledge, or control of the information and not upon
the prospective recipient. These principles are equally applicable

10.1 General. Reproduction of classified material shall be approved by the Security Officer. Top Secret information cannot be reproduced without the originator's written consent.

A. Top Secret material shall be destroyed only by the Department Top Secret Control Officer.
B. Secret and Confidential material, for which controls are required by the originator, shall be destroyed by two appropriately cleared employees. Dissemination Control Markings for Classified and CUI
seltz.snippet:
Dissemination control markings are labels added to government documents that tell every person handling them who is allowed to see the information and how it may be shared. They appear on both classified national security information and Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI), and they carry legal force. A document’s classification level alone never tells the full story about access; the dissemination controls stacked next to it do.

## The Classification Levels Underneath

Dissemination controls sit on top of a classification decision, so the levels are worth naming first. Executive Order 13526 establishes three tiers based on the damage unauthorized disclosure would cause to national security: Confidential (damage), Secret (serious damage), and Top Secret (exceptionally grave damage).1National Archives. Executive Order 13526

The classification level sets the baseline clearance a reader needs. The dissemination control marking then adds a further restriction. A document marked SECRET//NOFORN requires both a Secret clearance and the additional rule that no foreign national may access it, cleared or not.

On classified documents, dissemination controls appear after the classification level in the banner line, separated by double slashes. Three appear routinely in intelligence and defense work.
